root_cause.text: The mt76 driver failed to destroy page_pools and return pages for WED RRO RX queues during device destruction (module unload) because the cleanup routine (mt76_dma_cleanup) unconditionally skipped all WED RRO queues when WED was active, even though those queues had allocated page_pools that needed to be freed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `continue` that skipped WED RRO queues in `mt76_dma_cleanup`, and adjusts `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup` to only skip returning pages for those queues when WED is active and the queue is a specific WED RRO sub-type (e.g., `mt76_queue_is_wed_rro_rxdmad_c` or `mt76_queue_is_wed_rro_ind`), ensuring that page_pools are destroyed and pages are returned appropriately. The commit message explicitly states: "All MT76 rx queues have an associated page_pool even if the queue is not associated to a NAPI ... Destroy the page_pool running mt76_dma_cleanup routine during module unload."

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition guards the call to mt76_put_page_pool_buf, causing it to be skipped for WED RRO queues, preventing freeing of page pool buffers.
This call is only executed for non-WED RRO queues due to the preceding condition, so page pool buffers for WED RRO are not freed during cleanup, leading to memory leak.
